question.leadin: This conflict began due to a dispute over whether Native Americans should be driven out of Virginia.
question.text: Name this 1676 rebellion against colonial governor William Berkeley. It collapsed after its namesake died of dysentery.
question.clue: The leader of one side during this event attempted to ally with Cockacoeske ("ka-ka-ko-ESS-kee"), the "Queen of Pamunkey."

swap.text: Twenty people were executed for being associated with the Devil during these series of hearings. Arthur Miller wrote about these events in The Crucible.
swap.clue: These events were recorded in a book titled Wonders of the Invisible World by Cotton Mather, who influenced the execution of Ann Glover.

question.leadin: This publication predicted the death of Titan Leeds in 1732. Leeds wasn't dead in 1733, but this publication printed an obituary anyway; when Leeds protested, this publication suspected an imposter.
question.text: Name this annual publication, filled with astronomical information, poems, proverbs, and a calendar, that was extremely popular in the American colonies.
question.clue: Naval hero John Paul Jones named his ship after this publication.

swap.leadin: The war saw the British under Anson attacking the Manila Galleon, after which he circumnavigated the globe.
swap.text: Identify this war that saw the battles at Porto Bello and Cartagena that was sparked by the Spanish seizure of its namesake's ship, Rebecca.
swap.clue: Seeing an unsuccessful amphibious assault on Cartagena de Indias, the incident that sparked this war involved the boarding of the ship Rebecca.

question.leadin: It was built by Contrecoeur in 1754 to secure the Ohio Valley during the French and Indian War.
question.text: Name this French fort in Pennsylvania which was the target of the Braddock expedition, which turned into a fiasco. Fort Necessity was built to increase British power in the region so that an attack on this fort could occur.
question.clue: This place was part of a series of fortifications including Fort Machault and Fort Le Boeuf.

swap.text: Ivar the Boneless conquered this city, which then became the center of the Danelaw. This city was the birthplace of the scholar Alcuin, who was the head of the palace school at Aachen.
swap.clue: A scholar born in this city devised the first Western European script with lower-case letters and spacing between words and headed the palace school at Aachen.

question.text: The Proclamation of 1763 was issued after the end of this war, the North American theater of the Seven Years' War.
question.clue: Dissatisfaction with the result of this war led to Pontiac's Rebellion.

swap.leadin: Name these European explorers of the Western Hemisphere.
swap.text: This man completed the first documented crossing of the Mississippi River by a European. Francisco Pizarro sent this man to invite the Incan emperor Atahualpa to a meeting.
swap.clue: This man's death saw him succeeded by Luis de Moscosco Alvarado, who led his men southwest into Texas at the end of this man's expedition.

question.text: Winthrop banished this fiery preacher, who went on to found a colony at Rhode Island.
question.clue: Earlier in his life, he chafed at Archbishop William Laud's strict control of Anglican Church doctrine, escaping with his wife Mary to Boston.

swap.leadin: Its first assembly was presided over by George Yeardley, who had earlier participated in the ill-fated Third Supply Mission.
swap.text: Name this legislative body, the first such body in the British Colonies. White landowning men over 17 had the right to vote in members, and in 1699 it was moved to Williamsburg.
swap.clue: Distinguished members included Captain Francis West and Reverend William Wickham.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Horatio Nelson.
question.text: In 1784, Nelson was sent to the area near Antigua to enforce these acts, which restricted foreign vessels from trading with England or its colonies.
question.clue: Repealed officially in 1849, they were accompanied by the Staple Act and targeted items subject to "enumeration."

swap.leadin: Name these people associated with the founding of American colonies.
swap.text: In 1638, this Puritan leader spearheaded the creation of the first colonial constitution, his colony's Fundamental Orders.
swap.clue: Thomas Welles and Roger Ludlow drafted a document inspired by this man's theories which was signed by the cities of Wethersfield and Windsor and which guaranteed universal manhood suffrage.

question.text: The Brown family sponsored Esek Hopkins on a disastrous 1764 voyage of a slave ship with this name. A 1998 DNA test supported Annette Gordon-Reed's theory about an enslaved woman with this first name.

swap.text: As an apprentice, Benjamin Franklin printed the New-England Courant newspaper, which featured this female persona of his giving humorous accounts of colonial life.
swap.clue: Benjamin Franklin, who wrote Poor Richard's Almanack, had earlier written in the New England Courant under this pseudonym. 14 letters published in 1722 were attributed to Franklin under this pseudonym.

question.leadin: Give some answers about a colony that didn't make it into the original thirteen United States.
question.text: This innovation of Reverend Solomon Stoddard created a tier of church membership whose requirements were less onerous for less pious descendants of the original New England settlers.
question.clue: This relaxation of church policy in colonial New England which allowed second and third generation settlers to gain partial membership.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Fort Mose, the first free Black settlement to be officially sanctioned in the American colonies.
swap.text: The possibility of fleeing to Fort Mose likely inspired the leaders of this slave rebellion to seek freedom. This slave rebellion in South Carolina was led by people from Kongo.
swap.clue: During this event, participants marched toward Spanish Florida from South Carolina carrying a banner that read "Liberty!"

question.leadin: Identify these preachers active during the Great Awakening FTPE.
question.text: This priest of Boston's First Church was the staunchest opponent of the Great Awakening and warned against believing itinerant preachers. His most famous sermon was Enthusiasm Described and Cautioned Against.
question.clue: Both Whitefield and Edwards were attacked by this Boston divine, whose 1742 sermon Enthusiasm Described and Cautioned Against saw in the Awakening the legacy of the Munster Anabaptists and Antinomians.

swap.leadin: This association created a five-member court to run its territory chaired by John Carter, and negotiated with Cherokee Indians to make the Transylvania Purchase.
swap.text: Name this association which, in 1772, established an autonomous republic on the banks of the namesake river in Tennessee when they realized they were living south of the official territory of North Carolina.

question.text: The revolt was crushed at this two-hour battle, where the Regulators told Tryon to "fire and be damned" after being told to lay down their arms.

swap.leadin: Name these events from early relations between Colonial America and the Native Americans.
swap.text: Much earlier, Powhatan Confederacy instigated this siege against the Jamestown Colony in the winter of 1609, which led to them temporarily abandoning the colony entirely and sailing back to England.
swap.clue: A major cause of this period, during which some relief came from trade with the Nansemonds, was the failure of the Third Supply due to the wreck of the Sea Venture, an event which inspired The Tempest.
